artifact.canonical_name: Building Automotive Security on Internet Standards: An Integration of DNSSEC, DANE, and DANCE to Authenticate and Authorize In-Car Services

sources.title: Building Automotive Security on Internet Standards: An Integration of DNSSEC, DANE, and DANCE to Authenticate and Authorize In-Car Services
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The proposal separates supplier-side software/certificate generation from OEM-controlled deployment trust by publishing supplier certificates through OEM-signed DNSSEC TLSA records.

DNSSEC, DANE and DANCE are integrated into automotive publish-subscribe service discovery/authentication/authorization, with an example SOME/IP integration and support for cached/offline verification.
The authors evaluate the design using a STRIDE threat analysis and a realistic in-vehicle setup; the evaluation indicates service setup remains below their cited 200-ms requirement despite jitter.
claims.context: Author security/performance evaluation, not independent certification.

metrics.name: approximate DNSSEC records per vehicle zone
metrics.context: Scale estimate reported from the realistic IVN evaluation.

metrics.name: average TLSA certificates resolved per node for remote peers
service setup requirement referenced by evaluation
metrics.context: Authors report individual-service setup well below this cited requirement.

limitations.text: The evaluation shows high performance jitter, attributed partly to parallel execution on a single system; Open vSwitch/Mininet emulation also omits physical network transmission times.
Supply-chain attacks, secure builds, OTA distribution and some mixed-security downgrade cases are outside the detailed security analysis.
The main automotive evaluation does not include remote DNSSEC resolution in the service-setup path; the authors expect such resolution to occur during update procedures.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Building Automotive Security on Internet Standards: An Integration of DNSSEC, DANE, and DANCE to Authenticate and Authorize In-Car Services; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The full primary text verifies the DNSSEC/DANE/DANCE trust model, SOME/IP integration, STRIDE analysis, realistic-IVN evaluation, scale figures and explicit jitter/simulation/security-scope limitations.

editorial.why_now_note: As SOA and post-sale software increase multi-supplier dynamism, credential ownership and service authorization become first-class architecture boundaries rather than fixed provisioning details.
editorial.rationale: Strong service/security architecture evidence: it explicitly separates supplier credentials from OEM deployment trust and evaluates a protocol-independent credential lifecycle integrated with SOME/IP.
